pr.title: Count every review in a private repository
pr.head: 808eb63c4a9303b72a58cd346e0db6c69894236f

summary: Projector decides whether a pull request is signed off from the newest Projector review on its head: a GitHub review whose body carries a hidden marker naming the verdict, the head it read, and the model that wrote it. Two places read those reviews. The CLI's project review status and the draft-state step of project review publish read them through verdicts, and the Projector site's deploy reads them through review_statuses to show each pull request as Clean, Changes requested, or Unreviewed.

Until now both counted a review only when GitHub reported its author's association, GitHub's author_association, as OWNER, MEMBER, or COLLABORATOR, because anyone can review a public repository's pull request. The site's deploy asks GitHub with the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN, which cannot see a private organization membership, so in a company's private repository GitHub reported members' reviews to that token with a lower association. The site dropped every verdict and showed every pull request as Unreviewed.

This change counts every review in a private or internal repository, where only an account that can see the repository can review at all, and keeps the association check in a public repository. One helper, review_counts, holds the rule, and both readers ask GitHub for the repository's visibility, public, private, or internal, in a request they already make.

groups.title: One rule for whose reviews count
groups.kicker: A helper that decides from the association and the repository's visibility
intro: Before this change, verdicts in the CLI and review_statuses on the site each tested the association against the TRUSTED tuple themselves. The new review_counts(association, visibility) answers for both: it counts any review when the visibility is private or internal, in either letter case, and otherwise falls back to the association test.

GraphQL reports visibility in capitals and REST in lowercase, which is why the helper lowercases it. A missing visibility counts as public, so a repository GitHub says nothing about keeps the strict rule.

files.note: Adds review_counts and repo_visibility, threads the visibility into verdicts, and moves publish's pull request fetch ahead of the verdict read so one response serves both.

checks.text: Reverting this line to association in TRUSTED makes the six new tests fail with ten subtest failures; at the head the full suite passes, 835 tests with one skip.
The CLI reads the base repository's visibility from the REST pull request it already fetches, base.repo.visibility. For this repository GitHub returns public.
Fetching current before the verdicts rather than after leaves the hold lookup and the draft comparison below reading the same response as before.

files.note: Covers publish's draft state and status in private, internal, and public repositories, and the helper's case handling.

groups.title: The site reads the visibility with the reviews
groups.kicker: The status query asks for the repository's visibility and passes it to the rule
intro: The site gets each pull request's state and reviews from summary.pr_status, one paged GraphQL query. The query now also asks for repository.visibility, returns it lowercased as visibility, and build_summaries hands it to review_statuses, so a private repository's deploy counts its members' reviews again.

files.note: Adds visibility to the status query and its result.

checks.text: Running pr_status against this repository's pull request 260 through gh printed public ['OWNER'], so the query and its jq filter return the visibility.

files.note: Passes the visibility from the status lookup to review_statuses, which calls review_counts in place of its own TRUSTED test.

checks.text: The = None default is unused: the one caller always passes the value, and leaving it out silently gives the strict public rule.
A status without visibility, as from an older lookup, reads as None and keeps the association check.

Checks the query asks for the visibility and lowercases it.

groups.kicker: The CLI reference and the review-pr skill
intro: docs/cli.md describes whose verdicts the site, publish, and status count, and the review-pr skill says the same for the draft-state step. Each now gives the public rule and the private or internal rule.
